title: AI Infra Provider Yotta Eyes $1.5 Bn IPO By March 2027: Report
title_bn: এআই ইনফ্রা প্রোভাইডার ইয়ট্টার ২০২৭ সালের মার্চের মধ্যে ১.৫ বিলিয়ন ডলারের আইপিও প্রত্যাশাঃ রিপোর্ট
author: TechPulse
excerpt: After ESDS, AI data centre provider Yotta Data Services is now eyeing to go public and plans to file its…
paragraph1: SUMMARYYotta Data Services plans to file its draft IPO papers in October and launch its IPO in the January-March quarter of 2027 The company will raise up to $1.5 Bn through a fresh issue of shares from its IPO, using the capital to repay debt, purchase GPUs, and expand its sovereign cloud infrastructure Yotta plans to invest over $7 Bn on AI infrastructure by the end of FY27 and has already raised $150 Mn to fund its expenditure After ESDS, AI data centre provider Yotta Data Services is now eyeing to go public and plans to file its draft IPO papers with the SEBI by October. The company is looking to go public within the March quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q4 FY27), CEO Sunil Gupta told Reuters. The company is eyeing the raise of up to $1.
paragraph2: 5 Bn from its IPO, which is likely to solely comprise a fresh issue of equity shares. CEO Gupta told the publication that the capital will be used to repay debt, purchase graphics processing units (GPUs), and expand sovereign cloud infrastructure to address surging local AI computing demand. Inc42 has reached out to Yotta seeking comments on the development. The story will be updated based on their responses.
paragraph3: The Hiranandani Group-backed firm, which positions itself as India’s largest provider of NVIDIA-powered AI computing infrastructure, has already raised $150 Mn from non-institutional investors at a valuation of $3.9 Bn. Founded in 2019 by Gupta and Darshan Hiranandani, Yotta started out as a colocation centre and integrated data centre services provider. It now earns 20% of its revenue from colocation, 25-30% from sovereign cloud and managed services, and about 50% from GPUs, Gupta told Inc42 recently.
paragraph4: While it had earlier catered primarily to Indian startups and institutions like IIT Bombay and IIT Madras, Yotta has pivoted to focusing on international customers from whom it can extract higher pricing. They currently account for 75-80% of Yotta’s customer base, per the Reuters report. The Centre’s tax holiday for foreign companies that are providing cloud services globally while using data centre services from India has helped the company shift its customer mix towards global customers, according to Gupta. Yotta has planned to spend over $7 Bn on AI infrastructure by the end of FY27, out of which $4 Bn has already been committed.
paragraph5: To support its expansion while offsetting the high cost of GPU acquisition, it is exploring financing structures where its customers fund and own the GPUs. Yotta would subsequently share the revenue generated by the hardware with the partner (with around 75% going to the partner and 25% to Yotta), and then buy them back at market value.
bangla_paragraph1: সংক্ষিপ্তসারYotta ডেটা সার্ভিসেস অক্টোবরে তার খসড়া আইপিও কাগজপত্র জমা দেওয়ার পরিকল্পনা করেছে এবং 2027 সালের জানুয়ারি-মার্চ ত্রৈমাসিকে তার আইপিओ চালু করবে। কোম্পানিটি তার আইপির শেয়ারের একটি নতুন ইস্যু করে 1.5 বিলিয়ন ডলার পর্যন্ত সংগ্রহ করবে, debtণ পরিশোধ, জিপিইউ কেনার জন্য মূলধন ব্যবহার করবে এবং তার সার্বভৌম মেঘ অবকাঠামো প্রসারিত করবে।
bangla_paragraph2: ইন্ক 42 ইয়োটাকে যোগাযোগ করেছে এবং এই বিষয়ে মন্তব্যের জন্য অনুরোধ করেছে। তাদের প্রতিক্রিয়ার ভিত্তিতে গল্পটি আপডেট করা হবে।
bangla_paragraph3: The Hiranandani Group-backed firm, which positions itself as India’s largest provider of NVIDIA-powered AI computing infrastructure, has already raised $150 Mn from non-institutional investors at a valuation of $3.9 Bn. Founded in 2019 by Gupta and Darshan Hiranandani, Yotta started out as a colocation centre and integrated data centre services provider. It now earns 20% of its revenue from colocation, 25-30% from sovereign cloud and managed services, and about 50% from GPUs, Gupta told Inc42 recently.
bangla_paragraph4: যদিও এটি পূর্বে প্রাথমিকভাবে আইআইটি বোম্বাই এবং আইআইটির মতো ভারতীয় স্টার্টআপস এবং প্রতিষ্ঠানগুলির জন্য পরিবেশন করেছিল, ইয়ট্টার দৃষ্টি আকর্ষণ করা হয়েছে আন্তর্জাতিক গ্রাহকদের উপর যাদের থেকে এটি উচ্চ মূল্য অর্জন করতে পারে। তারা বর্তমানে রয়টার্স রিপোর্টের মতে ইয়টটার গ্রাহক বেসের 75-80%। কেন্দ্রের বিদেশী সংস্থাগুলির জন্য করের ছুটি যা বিশ্বব্যাপী ক্লাউড পরিষেবা সরবরাহ করছে যখন ভারত থেকে ডেটা সেন্টার পরিষেবাগুলি ব্যবহার করে সংস্থাটি তার গ্রাহক মিশ্রণকে বিশ্বব্যাপি গ্রাহকদের দিকে স্থানান্তরিত করতে সহায়তা করেছে।
bangla_paragraph5: জিপিইউ অধিগ্রহণের উচ্চ ব্যয়কে কমিয়ে আনার সাথে সাথে তার সম্প্রসারণকে সমর্থন করার জন্য, এটি অর্থায়ন কাঠামো অনুসন্ধান করছে যেখানে এর গ্রাহকরা জিপিআইগুলিকে তহবিল এবং মালিকানাধীন করে। ইয়োটা পরবর্তীকালে হার্ডওয়্যার দ্বারা উত্পন্ন রাজস্ব অংশীদারদের সাথে ভাগ করবে (প্রায় 75% অংশীদারের কাছে এবং 25% ইয়োটার কাছে), এবং তারপরে তাদের বাজার মূল্যে ফিরে কিনবে।

title: Fractal Define One case review: Balancing noise and thermals

excerpt: Fractal’s Define One rounds off the boxy Define, while still keeping the iconic closed-front design. A focus on GPU airflow and three included Momentum 14 fans highlight this $154 mid-tower chassis.
paragraph1: Fractal hits the nail on the head with the Define One, balancing quiet, cool, and premium looks. Smart details make it an easy recommendation at $154.99. Pros +Premium, conservative aesthetic with rounded edges +Integrated air guide results in great GPU temps +Integrated GPU support bracket +Includes three 140mm fans +Quiet operation Cons -Closed front limits airflow Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test. Go to page: The Fractal Define series has been around since 2009, starting with the aptly named Fractal Define chassis. Since then, we’ve seen the Define R2/R3/R4/R5/R6/R7/7 XL cases over the years, all keeping the familiar closed-front design. Today, Fractal released the Define One, which they say is a “...modern expression of quiet performance and Scandinavian aesthetics”. This ‘expression’ includes aluminum side intake vents, premium details, and subtle curves that aim for a clean, understated look balancing airflow and thermal efficiency.The new Define One achieves Fractal’s goals, offering users a clean, premium-looking chassis that achieves sound mitigation with its closed-front design. The previous Define 7 and 7 XL (and others before it) are all cuboids with sharp edges, whereas the Define One rounds the corners off for a softer, yet still premium appearance. This is one of the best-looking Define chassis to date.Inside, there’s room for large graphics cards, multiple radiators (up to 360mm), and it even supports rear-connect motherboards.
paragraph2: Fractal includes three pre-installed Momentum 14 fans in the front and has a unique integrated front air guide that feeds air directly from the bottom fan towards the video card. The interior is well thought out, with toolless access, removable brackets, and built-in cable management that makes building easier and leaves you with a clean, functional PC. Priced at $154.99, it gives off premium vibes you don’t normally find at this price point, or in previous Define iterations.We'll cover many more details inside and outside the chassis, showcasing the features and any issues we may encounter during the build process. We also run the case through thermal and noise testing to show how it performs compared to others and whether it has a chance of making our best PC cases list. Below are the case's specifications from Fractal.Define One Product Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally Type Mid-Tower Dimensions (H x L x W) 19.6 x 18.9 x 9.2-inches (500 x 482 x 235mm) Motherboard Support Mini-ITX, Micro ATX, ATX, E-ATX Back-connect Motherboard Support No Color Dark Solid Dark TG Light TintLight SolidLight TG Clear Tint Storage Support (2) 3.5-inch -or- (4) 2.5-inch(Supports up to six 2.5-inch total) PCIe Expansion Slots 7 Fan Support Top - 2x120/140mmFront - 3x120/140mmBottom - N/ARear - 1x120mm Pre-installed fans (3) 140mm LCP Blade Momentum 14 (Front) Radiator Support Front - Up to 360mmTop - Up to 280mmRear - 1x120mm CPU Cooler Clearance 171mm GPU Clearance 368mm (w/ front fans installed)338mm (w/ 30 thick front rad.
paragraph3: installed) Vertical GPU Support Yes (required adapter, $79.99) PSU Length 180mm Dust Filters Top, Front, Bottom Other features 3x included fans, integrated GPU front air guide, noise/vibration dampening MSRP $154.99 (all four configurations) Warranty 2 Years Features of the Define One▶️ External FeaturesExternally, the case looks considerably different than previous versions. While it still screams "computer case," those rounded edges soften the look of the closed-front design. The IO panel is still on top, and there’s a single LED at the top of the front panel, like previous designs. Another holdover is the ability to take the chassis apart for easy access, a boon for building. Overall, I do like the look of the 'Light' colorway. The subtle rounding off of sharp edges makes the Define One stand out among past iterations. It comes in four flavors: Dark (black) and Light (off-white) with closed sides, or Dark with tinted tempered glass and Light with tempered glass and no tint – one should match your style and build preferences. Image 1 of 7 (Image credit: Future) The side of the off-white Light case uses a clear tempered glass panel, secured by three tabs at the bottom and held to the frame by two ball-and-socket latching mechanisms on top. Slot the glass in and push on top and you're done. The clear glass allows for unobstructed views of the internals and easy access to the components inside. The other side panel is solid and bitumen-lined for sound dampening (like the front panel), and it attaches the same way, with tabs at the bottom and ball-and-socket mechanisms on top. Both have a small indentation at the top and rear of the case where you can easily grab and remove the panels.
paragraph4: Intake also comes through the sides. Two aluminum strips run vertically with small circular perforations, and on the Light chassis, the strips contrast with the rest of the off-white case and look good, breaking up the otherwise all-white colorway. These intakes also use a removable dust filter, accessible from the inside when you take off the front panel. It’s not the best situation for high airflow, but as we’ll see later, the Define One didn’t do a terrible job in our testing, especially on the GPU, using only one additional case fan, leaving the top empty.Turning the chassis around to the rear, we get a better view of the seven expansion slots (which also have a cover over the screws to clean up the appearance), the rear fan location supporting 120mm air movers, and the PSU mounting location at the bottom. The power supply uses a bracket with two captive thumbscrews. Simply mount it to your power supply, then install it in the case. Looking on the left, you’ll also see a couple of pre-installed Velcro straps to help with internal wire management.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.The bottom of the Define One uses a raised gray plastic frame that circles the entire bottom, with rubber ‘feet’ on the corners, giving your power supply about an inch of room to breathe. The dust filter on the bottom pulls out from the left side (window side), which is ideal since you likely won’t have to move your PC to remove it. In many cases, it comes out from the rear, requiring you to move your heavy PC to clean it. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Future) On top of the case, Fractal updated the design with a dense pattern of circular holes for air to pass through. This feels a bit more restrictive than the more open design on the Define 7, but still allowed air to escape even without fans on top in our testing.
paragraph5: The good news, at least when this area is used as exhaust, is that there isn’t a mesh dust filter to thwart airflow further. The top panel also pops off easily (via more ball-and-socket retention clips) from the back, exposing the inner frame where you mount fans or a radiator.The IO panel sits at the front edge and offers your typical assortment of ports. You get three USB ports: one USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 20 Gbps Type-C, and two USB 3.1 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) Type-A ports. This is exactly what we want to see in a case of this caliber. There’s also a shiny power button with the Fractal symbol in the middle, a 3.5mm combo audio jack on the left, and finally a skinny LED light at the top. The front panel also comes off easily. Removing the top panel exposes two levers, so you can remove the front panel, access the front of the case, and reach those three 140mm Momentum 14 fans and dust filters.▶️ Internal FeaturesInside the case, you have two separate chambers. One is for the power supply and cables, while the other is for the components.

title: Mac Studio Buyer's Guide: M5 Max vs. M5 Ultra
title_bn: ম্যাক স্টুডিও ক্রেতা গাইডঃ এম৫ ম্যাক্স বনাম এম৫ আল্ট্রা
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple last week announced two new Mac Studio models, with one built around the M5 Max chip and one around the all-new M5 Ultra chip, replacing the M4 Max and M3 Ultra models that had been on sale since March 2025. The gap between the two is unusually
paragraph1: Apple last week announced two new Mac Studio models, with one built around the M5 Max chip and one around the all-new M5 Ultra chip, replacing the M4 Max and M3 Ultra models that had been on sale since March 2025. The gap between the two is unusually wide this time. ‌Mac Studio‌ with M5 Max starts at $2,499, holding the price Apple set when it raised Mac prices in June, while ‌Mac Studio‌ with M5 Ultra starts at $5,499, a further $200 increase on the post-June M3 Ultra price and $1,500 above what the M3 Ultra cost at launch. That makes the premium $3,000 before any configure-to-order options, and memory and storage upgrades are more expensive than usual because of the memory chip shortage. Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two ‌Mac Studio‌ models is best for you. The shared features include: An identical enclosure measuring 3.7 inches tall and 7.7 inches wide Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing Hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, plus AV1 decode A next-generation SSD architecture that Apple says is up to twice as fast as before Thunderbolt 5 with up to 120Gb/s of bandwidth, and clustering of multiple systems using RDMA (remote direct memory access) 10Gb Ethernet, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot (UHS-II) Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 via the N1 chip, both new to the ‌Mac Studio‌ Genlock over USB-C for synchronization with professional camera capture A 3.
paragraph2: 5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones macOS 27, Apple Intelligence, and Siri AI Here is everything that differs between the two models: ‌Mac Studio‌ (M5 Max) ‌Mac Studio‌ (M5 Ultra) Starts at $2,499 Starts at $5,499 M5 Max chip M5 Ultra chip 18-core CPU with 6 super cores and 12 performance cores Up to 36-core CPU with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, from 30 cores Up to 40-core GPU, from 32 cores Up to 80-core GPU, from 64 cores 16-core Neural Engine 32-core Neural Engine Up to 614GB/s memory bandwidth 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth 36GB, 48GB, 64GB, or 128GB of unified memory 96GB, 256GB, or 512GB of unified memory 512GB, 1TB, 2TB, 4TB, or 8TB of storage 1TB, 2TB, 4TB, 8TB, or 16TB of storage Up to 3.9x faster AI performance than M4 Max Up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance of M3 Ultra Up to 50% faster graphics than M4 Max Up to 1.8x faster graphics than M3 Ultra One video decode engine and two video encode engines Two video decode engines and four video encode engines Two ProRes encode and decode engines Four ProRes encode and decode engines Four Thunderbolt 5 ports, two USB-C ports, and two USB-A ports Six Thunderbolt 5 ports and two USB-A ports Support for up to five 4K displays, four 6K displays, or two 8K displays Support for up to eight 4K displays, eight 6K displays, or four 8K displays 6.0 pounds (2.7 kg) 8.0 pounds (3.6 kg) For the overwhelming majority of buyers, including most professionals, the M5 Max is the more appropriate choice.
paragraph3: An 18-core CPU, up to 40 GPU cores with Neural Accelerators, up to 128GB of unified memory, and up to 614GB/s of bandwidth cover workflows such as multi-stream 4K and 6K editing, large Logic sessions with real-time plugins, compiling substantial codebases, and most 3D and motion work. Apple's own figures support this, with up to 3x faster Magic Mask performance in Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Studio and 1.4x faster scene rendering in Maxon Redshift compared to M4 Max, and graphics that are up to 50% faster than the previous generation. Since memory cannot be added later, the sensible approach is to spend more on unified memory at the point of purchase rather than on the higher chip tier. You should only choose the M5 Ultra if you anticipate running into a performance ceiling the M5 Max cannot clear. The most obvious use-case is local AI inference, where the whole model needs to be resident in memory. 256GB and 512GB configurations paired with 1.2TB/s of bandwidth allow models with hundreds of billions of parameters to run on the machine itself, which keeps sensitive material on-device and eliminates the recurring cost of paying for cloud inference. The other workflows that can take advantage of the M5 Ultra include studios finishing 8K material from several cameras at once, where the doubled Media Engine and its four encode engines earn their keep, research and simulation work that needs an enormous memory pool, and anyone who specifically needs six Thunderbolt 5 ports or more than five displays.
paragraph4: There is a notable catch in how the two memory ladders overlap. The M5 Ultra begins at 96GB, which is less than the 128GB you can configure on the M5 Max, so paying the premium at the entry configuration buys you more cores and more bandwidth, but less memory. The Ultra only separates itself at 256GB and above, and Apple limits the 512GB option to the 80-core GPU model, which means the configurations that justify the machine sit far above its starting price. This is where the price proximity argument becomes noticeable. Configuring an M5 Max with memory and storage narrows the gap considerably, and at that point the Ultra becomes worth pricing alongside it, because it roughly doubles GPU cores, Neural Engine cores, memory bandwidth, and Media Engine capacity in one step. If your workload sits comfortably inside 128GB, though, that money is better spent on storage and displays than on the chip. Both models support clustering over Thunderbolt 5 and RDMA, and Apple says four ‌Mac Studio‌ systems working together deliver up to 3x faster AI inference than a single machine, so scaling inference does not necessarily mean buying the most expensive configuration outright. If the M5 Max still looks like more performance than you need, the new Mac mini with the M5 Pro chip starts at $1,699 with up to a 20-core GPU and 307GB/s of memory bandwidth, which is enough for a great deal of professional work. Both new ‌Mac Studio‌ models are available to pre-order now, with availability beginning on September 22.
paragraph5: The 512GB configuration arrives in late October, and its pricing is expected to start well above $10,000. title: Flipkart Eyes Microdrama Entry Amid Diversification Push
title_bn: ফ্লিপকার্ট আইস মাইক্রোড্রামা এন্ট্রি
author: TechPulse
excerpt: On an experimentation spree, Walmart-owned Flipkart is now looking to enter the entertainment business with short-form scripted shows, microdramas. Sources…
paragraph1: SUMMARYFlipkart is testing a microdrama feed on its main app and is in talks with TTT, Pratilipi and other content creators to produce exclusive short-form shows, while also tapping Pinkvilla for content Flipkart’s microdrama play could eventually go beyond increasing time spent on the app, with the company potentially looking to connect content consumption with commerce The company entered quick commerce with Flipkart Minutes in 2024 and has since been exploring other parts of consumers’ daily lives, including food delivery and ticketing for films and live events On an experimentation spree, Walmart-owned Flipkart is now looking to enter the entertainment business with short-form scripted shows, microdramas. Sources told Inc42 that the ecommerce major is looking to partner with startups like Terribly Tiny Tales, Pratilipi, among others, to produce microdramas exclusively for its platform. Flipkart is also expected to source content from its digital media arm, Pinkvilla, which was acquired in 2025 for an undisclosed amount. As part of the broader content push, Vivek Mohan Sharma, business head – youth, music & english entertainment at JioStar, has been roped in as the CEO of Pinkvilla, replacing founder Nandini Shenoy, sources told Inc42. Inc42 has reached out to Flipkart for comment on the development. The story would be updated based on their response. Moneycontrol was the first to report on the development.
paragraph2: The microdrama offering will be integrated into Flipkart’s main app rather than launched as a standalone platform. Flipkart is testing a dedicated microdrama feed within its app, featuring personalised sections such as “Today’s top pick for you”, “Recommended Favourites” and “Flipkart user’s pick”. The move comes as Flipkart looks to expand beyond ecommerce and build a broader consumer ecosystem around its more than 500 Mn registered users. Flipkart’s microdrama play could eventually go beyond increasing time spent on the app, with the company potentially looking to connect content consumption with commerce. “The idea is simple. Flipkart wants to keep users engaged on their app for a long time. Suppose you are watching a piece of content and then crave Diet Coke.
paragraph3: You can order it without leaving the app,” said a person aware of the development. The plans come amid a rapid growth in India’s microdrama market, which is set to reach ₹650 Cr by 2028. Platforms such as Kuku TV, Story TV, DashReels and Quick TV are competing with larger players including JioHotstar and Amazon MX Player. The microdrama push is part of Flipkart’s broader diversification attempt beyond its mainstay ecommerce platform. The company entered the quick commerce with Flipkart Minutes in 2024 and has since been exploring other parts of consumers’ daily lives, including food delivery and ticketing for films and live events. Earlier this year, sources told Inc42 that Flipkart planned to launch its food-delivery service in Bengaluru by mid-August, with restaurants expected to pay a commission of 10-11% on each order. That launch, however, is yet to materialise.
paragraph4: Flipkart has also reportedly been considering an entry into India’s movie and live events ticketing market ahead of a potential IPO. Reuters reported that the company was weighing a separate vertical for the business, setting it up to compete with BookMyShow and Eternal’s District. There has been little visible progress on either front so far. Taken together, the plans point to an increasingly expansive ambition at Flipkart: to move beyond being a place where people shop and become a platform that captures more of their time, attention and spending. Ecommerce, quick commerce, entertainment, food delivery and ticketing each offer another way of bringing consumers deeper into the same ecosystem. Flipkart’s Top Deck Churn Flipkart is also witnessing a fresh round of top deck churn, with two more vice presidents, Prathyusha Agarwal, VP and head of strategy, and Aakriti Chandra, VP overseeing talent recruitment for Ekart, exiting the company. This takes the total number of VP-level exits to at least four in the past 10 days, Money control reported, citing sources.
paragraph5: The exits come amid a broader organisational rejig at Flipkart. Amit Sood, VP of corporate finance and head of investor relations, has taken charge of the finance charter at Ekart. Earlier, Gunjan Bhartia, senior VP of business finance, and Amer Hussain, VP of supply chain for Flipkart Grocery and Minutes. The departures follow several other senior-level changes across the Flipkart group, including CEO Nandita Sinha’s exit from Myntra and Flipkart Group CFO Sriram Venkatraman stepping down.

Sources told Inc42 that the ecommerce major is looking to partner with startups like Terribly Tiny Tales, Pratilipi, among others, to produce microdramas exclusively for its platform. Flipkart is also expected to source content from its digital media arm, Pinkvilla, which was acquired in 2025 for an undisclosed amount. As part of the broader content push, Vivek Mohan Sharma, business head – youth, music & english entertainment at JioStar, has been roped in as the CEO of Pinkvilla, replacing founder Nandini Shenoy, sources told Inc42. Inc42 has reached out to Flipkart for comment on the development. The story would be updated based on their response. Moneycontrol was the first to report on the development.
bangla_paragraph2: The microdrama offering will be integrated into Flipkart’s main app rather than launched as a standalone platform. Flipkart is testing a dedicated microdrama feed within its app, featuring personalised sections such as “Today’s top pick for you”, “Recommended Favourites” and “Flipkart user’s pick”. The move comes as Flipkart looks to expand beyond ecommerce and build a broader consumer ecosystem around its more than 500 Mn registered users. Flipkart’s microdrama play could eventually go beyond increasing time spent on the app, with the company potentially looking to connect content consumption with commerce. “The idea is simple. Flipkart wants to keep users engaged on their app for a long time. Suppose you are watching a piece of content and then crave Diet Coke.
bangla_paragraph3: You can order it without leaving the app,” said a person aware of the development. The plans come amid a rapid growth in India’s microdrama market, which is set to reach ₹650 Cr by 2028. Platforms such as Kuku TV, Story TV, DashReels and Quick TV are competing with larger players including JioHotstar and Amazon MX Player. The microdrama push is part of Flipkart’s broader diversification attempt beyond its mainstay ecommerce platform. The company entered the quick commerce with Flipkart Minutes in 2024 and has since been exploring other parts of consumers’ daily lives, including food delivery and ticketing for films and live events. Earlier this year, sources told Inc42 that Flipkart planned to launch its food-delivery service in Bengaluru by mid-August, with restaurants expected to pay a commission of 10-11% on each order. That launch, however, is yet to materialise.
bangla_paragraph4: Flipkart has also reportedly been considering an entry into India’s movie and live events ticketing market ahead of a potential IPO. Reuters reported that the company was weighing a separate vertical for the business, setting it up to compete with BookMyShow and Eternal’s District. There has been little visible progress on either front so far. Taken together, the plans point to an increasingly expansive ambition at Flipkart: to move beyond being a place where people shop and become a platform that captures more of their time, attention and spending. Ecommerce, quick commerce, entertainment, food delivery and ticketing each offer another way of bringing consumers deeper into the same ecosystem. Flipkart’s Top Deck Churn Flipkart is also witnessing a fresh round of top deck churn, with two more vice presidents, Prathyusha Agarwal, VP and head of strategy, and Aakriti Chandra, VP overseeing talent recruitment for Ekart, exiting the company. This takes the total number of VP-level exits to at least four in the past 10 days, Money control reported, citing sources.
bangla_paragraph5: The exits come amid a broader organisational rejig at Flipkart. Amit Sood, VP of corporate finance and head of investor relations, has taken charge of the finance charter at Ekart. Earlier, Gunjan Bhartia, senior VP of business finance, and Amer Hussain, VP of supply chain for Flipkart Grocery and Minutes. The departures follow several other senior-level changes across the Flipkart group, including CEO Nandita Sinha’s exit from Myntra and Flipkart Group CFO Sriram Venkatraman stepping down.

title: Simple Energy Launches Wave Family Escooter At ₹1.1 Lakh
title_bn: ১.১ লক্ষ টাকায় ওয়েভ ফ্যামিলি স্কুটার চালু করল সিম্পল এনার্জি
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler startup Simple Energy has launched its first family escooter, the Simple Wave, at an introductory starting price…
paragraph1: SUMMARYSimple Energy has launched its first family electric scooter, the Simple Wave, with six models across three variants starting at ₹1.10 Lakh. The launch comes as India’s E2W makers increasingly turn to affordable, commuter-focused scooters with practical range to expand beyond the premium early-adopter segment amid intensifying competition. The top-end Simple Wave+ offers a 243 km IDC range and 90 kmph top speed, while Simple Energy plans to scale monthly sales to 10,000 units by March 2027 from around 1,500 currently. Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler startup Simple Energy has launched its first family escooter, the Simple Wave, at an introductory starting price of ₹1.10 Lakh (ex-showroom). The lineup comprises six models across three variants: the Simple Wave S, Simple Wave, and Simple Wave+. All of them have different battery capacities, displays, and connected features. The top-end Simple Wave+ comes with a 5 kWh battery pack, an IDC-certified range of 243 km, and a top speed of 90 kmph.
paragraph2: It is powered by a 6.4 kW permanent magnet synchronous motor, which generates 179 Nm of wheel torque. The other models come with battery capacities of 3.7 kWh, 2.7 kWh, and 2.2 kWh, offering IDC-certified ranges of 171 km, 132 km, and 110 km, respectively. Bookings for the Simple Wave have opened across the startup’s stores and website, with deliveries scheduled to begin in the last week of September. The escooter range comes with portable chargers and supports both standard and fast charging. Simple Energy claimed that its top model supports 0-80% charging in a minimum 2 hours and 15 minutes.
paragraph3: Simple Energy’s Expansion Simple Energy was founded in 2019 by Rajkumar and Shreshth Mishra, while Ankit Gupta later joined the startup as a cofounder. It competes against Ola Electric, Ather Energy, TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto, and Hero MotorCorp in the electric two-wheeler segment. Simple Energy currently has the capacity to manufacture 3,000 scooters a month. The startup said it is currently selling around 1,500 escooters a month through more than 75 outlets across 63 cities. It plans to increase monthly sales to 10,000 units by March 2027 by expanding its production capacity and retail network. It expects its manufacturing capacity utilisation to rise to 75-80% by the end of the next financial year from around 35% currently. In June, the startup raised ₹250 Cr in a mix of debt and equity as it prepared to transition into a full-stack EV OEM and gear up for an IPO. Simple Energy plans to use the capital primarily to scale up manufacturing capacity and expand production, while the remaining funds will go toward sales, marketing, and R&D to strengthen its product roadmap and customer experience. Its investors include the family office of Thyrocare founder Arokiaswamy Velumani, Haran Family Office, Desai Family Office, and Vasavi Family Office.
paragraph4: The startup has raised more than $84 Mn to date. EV Launches Gather Pace The Simple Wave’s launch comes days after rivals Ola Electric and Ather Energy rolled out new scooters targeting the mass-market E2W segment. Last week, Ola Electric launched its S1Z escooter in two variants priced at ₹79,999 and ₹99,999. The variants offer IDC-certified ranges of 179 km and 301 km, respectively. The S1Z is Ola Electric’s first scooter range powered by its locally developed 46-series LFP Bharat Cell technology. Around the same time, Ather Energy launched the Konarc family escooter at a starting price of ₹99,999. The scooter, built on Ather’s new EL platform, comes in six variants across the S and Z product lines and offers IDC-certified range options of 100 km, 120 km, 165 km, and 200 km. The launches come as electric two-wheeler manufacturers increasingly focus on affordable models, practical range, and commuter-oriented designs to attract buyers beyond the premium early-adopter segment. As per Vahan data, electric two-wheeler registrations fell 16.
paragraph5: 2% MoM to 1.72 Lakh units in August from 2.05 Lakh units in July. However, registrations jumped 64% YoY from 1.05 Lakh units in August last year.

title: Galaxy S27 Ultra could go Exynos again, and this time, Snapdragon fans might get jealous
title_bn: গ্যালাক্সি এস২৭ আল্ট্রা আবার এক্সিনোস ব্যবহার করতে পারে, এবং এইবার স্ন্যাপড্রাগন ভক্তরা ঈর্ষান্বিত হতে পারে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Internal testing at Samsung shows Exynos 2700 outperforms the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro.
paragraph1: TL;DR Samsung might launch a Galaxy S27 Ultra variant with Exynos 2700 in some regions. Exynos 2700 is rumored to have outperformed the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro in Samsung’s internal testing. Along with the Ultra, the Galaxy S27 Pro could also come with the Exynos 2700 in certain markets. Samsung appears to be on track to launch the Galaxy S27 series early next year. The series gains a new Pro variant in addition to the three existing models, but the bigger, more polarizing change so far is the Galaxy S27 Ultra’s new camera bump, which would invariably remind you of the iPhone 17 (and 18) Pro.
paragraph2: Now, another surprising piece of news appears to raise the bar for the Galaxy S27’s surprises, and this one particularly talks about its innards.South Korean publication Money Today (via tipster Jukan) says Samsung will launch a Galaxy S27 Ultra variant driven by the Exynos 2700. The report notably contradicts previous claims (and natural assumptions) that the Ultra would only use a Snapdragon chip. If that proves true, it would be the first Ultra in the Galaxy S series to feature an Exynos chip since the Galaxy S22 Ultra five generations earlier.As with previous years, Samsung would not fully relinquish the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro (or whatever the new top-tier chip may be officially called).
paragraph3: Instead, it is said to take a dual-chip approach, offering Exynos 2700 on the Galaxy S27 Ultra in certain markets only. Buyers in the US will most likely continue to get a Snapdragon-powered Ultra.The decision may be backed by the reported performance upgrades of the Exynos 2700. Korean publication Yonhap News reported last month that Samsung has been testing the Exynos 2700 against the various Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 trims. According to these internal tests, the Exynos 2700 delivers 19% higher CPU performance than the Snapdragon 8 Gen 6 and roughly 10% better than the Pro variant.
paragraph4: Similar trends are supposedly seen across GPU and NPU benchmarks too.These numbers are supposedly based on Geekbench 6.5 tests. But as we know, benchmarks can be deceiving because they often don’t account for sustained usage. When we tested the Galaxy S26 Plus’ Exynos 2600 against the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, we found the Exynos to outperform the latter in benchmarks.
paragraph5: But the Exynos’s shortcomings were exposed when it started to heat up prematurely.Samsung could reportedly also use Exynos 2700 selectively on the Galaxy S27 Pro — just like the Ultra. Samsung is also expected to sell Exynos-powered Galaxy S27 and the Galaxy S27 Plus in certain markets, but that’s a relatively less surprising premise.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.
bangla_paragraph1: টিলারঃ ডঃ স্যামসাং কিছু অঞ্চলে এক্সিনোস ২700 সহ গ্যালাক্সি এস 27 আল্ট্রা ভেরিয়েন্ট চালু করতে পারে। এক্সিনস ২7০০ গুজব রয়েছে যে স্যামসুংয়ের অভ্যন্তরীণ পরীক্ষায় স্ন্যাপড্রাগন 8 এলিট জেনার 6 প্রোকে ছাড়িয়ে গেছে। আল্ট্রাসের পাশাপাশি, গ্যাল্যাক্সিএস 27 প্রো নির্দিষ্ট বাজারে এক্সিনোজ ২700 এর সাথে আসতে পারে। স্যামসং সম্ভবত আগামী বছরের শুরুতে গ্যালাকাসি এস ২7 সিরিজ চালু করার পথে রয়েছে। সিরিজটি তিনটি বিদ্যমান মডেলের পাশাপাশি একটি নতুন প্রো ভেরिएন্ট অর্জন করে, তবে এখন পর্যন্ত বৃহত্তর, আরও মেরুকরণ পরিবর্তন
bangla_paragraph2: এখন, আরেকটি বিস্ময়কর সংবাদ গ্যালাক্সি এস 27 এর বিস্ময়ের জন্য বারটি বাড়িয়ে তুলতে দেখা যাচ্ছে, এবং এটি বিশেষত এর অন্তর্নিহিত বিষয়ে কথা বলে। দক্ষিণ কোরিয়ার প্রকাশনা মানি টুডে (টিপস্টার জুকানের মাধ্যমে) বলেছে যে স্যামসাং এক্সিনোস 2700 দ্বারা চালিত একটি গ্যাল্যাক্সি S27 আল্ট্রা ভেরিয়েন্ট চালু করবে। প্রতিবেদনটি উল্লেখযোগ্যভাবে পূর্ববর্তী দাবিগুলির সাথে (এবং প্রাকৃতিক অনুমানগুলি) বিরোধিতা করে যে আল্ট্রাস কেবল স্ন্যাপড্রাগন চিপ ব্যবহার করবে। যদি এটি সত্য প্রমাণিত হয় তবে এটি গ্যালাকি এস সিরিজের প্রথম আল্ট্রামা হবে যা এক্সিনস চিপ বৈশিষ্ট্যযুক্ত হবে।
bangla_paragraph3: Instead, it is said to take a dual-chip approach, offering Exynos 2700 on the Galaxy S27 Ultra in certain markets only. Buyers in the US will most likely continue to get a Snapdragon-powered Ultra.The decision may be backed by the reported performance upgrades of the Exynos 2700. Korean publication Yonhap News reported last month that Samsung has been testing the Exynos 2700 against the various Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 trims. According to these internal tests, the Exynos 2700 delivers 19% higher CPU performance than the Snapdragon 8 Gen 6 and roughly 10% better than the Pro variant.
bangla_paragraph4: এই সংখ্যাগুলি গিকবেঞ্চ ৬.৫ পরীক্ষার উপর ভিত্তি করে। কিন্তু আমরা জানি, বেঞ্চমার্কগুলি প্রতারণামূলক হতে পারে কারণ তারা প্রায়শই স্থায়ী ব্যবহারের জন্য অ্যাকাউন্ট নেয় না। যখন আমরা গ্যালাক্সি এস২৬ প্লাস  এক্সিনোস ২৬০০ কে স্ন্যাপড্রাগন ৮ এলিট জেনার ৫ এর বিরুদ্ধে পরীক্ষা করেছি, তখন আমরা এক্সিনসকে বেঞ্চমেকে শেষের চেয়ে ভাল করতে দেখেছি।
bangla_paragraph5: তবে এক্সিনোসের ত্রুটিগুলি প্রকাশিত হয়েছিল যখন এটি অকাল গরম হতে শুরু করেছিল। স্যামসুং রিপোর্ট করা হয়েছে যে গ্যালাক্সি এস 27 প্রো  তে আল্ট্রার মতো এক্সিনস 2700 নির্বাচনযোগ্যভাবে ব্যবহার করতে পারে। সামসুং নির্দিষ্ট বাজারে এক্সিনোজ চালিত গ্যাল্যাক্সি S27 এবং গ্যালাসি S 27 প্লাস বিক্রি করবে বলে আশা করা হচ্ছে, তবে এটি তুলনামূলকভাবে কম বিস্ময়কর ধারণা। অনুসরণ করুনআমাদের সম্প্রদায়ের অংশ হওয়ার জন্য আপনাকে ধন্যবাদ। পোস্ট করার আগে আমাদের মন্তব্য নীতি পড়ুন।

title: The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 ergonomic chair automatically tracks your whole body
title_bn: সিহু ডোরো সি৩০০ প্রো ভি২ এরগনোমিক চেয়ার আপনার পুরো শরীরকে স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে ট্র্যাক করে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: No more fidgeting to find the best position when you sit.
paragraph1: SihooErgonomic chairs with support in the right places can make your day a lot more comfortable. The catch, unfortunately, is that no one sits in the exact same position the whole time. We lean forward to type, then recline to think for a second, then lean forward again, push back to stretch, and so much more. Meanwhile, you’re continuously trying to find the perfect position again.Most ergonomic chairs offer manual adjustments for multiple focus areas, with each needing its own changes. However, Sihoo treats every shift as one continuous motion and manages everything automatically. The Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 is one of the first full-body adaptive ergonomic chairs, built around a system that tracks your head, back, lumbar area, and arms as a group. Sihoo has been in the ergonomic chair business for 15 years, and the Doro C300 Pro V2 is its latest. Here’s what you need to know.DynaCore and SyncroFlex: tracking your body as a wholeSihooThe Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2’s DynaCore system keeps it all running. It uses real-time gravity sensing to track how your body is moving and coordinates the head, lumbar, back, and arm supports so they respond together. When you shift position, all four zones adjust at roughly the same time, so you don’t end up with support in one area and a gap in another.
paragraph2: The system is also linked to the armrests, and everything runs without any manual input.While DynaCore handles the chair coordination as a whole, the SyncroFlex system focuses on the backrest itself. It uses a dual-spring, dual-track structure that reads your spine curvature and lets the backrest glide along with it as you move. The chair conforms to your body as soon as you sit down – no manual setting adjustments required – and the lumbar support slides with your center of gravity to maintain contact through the recline.SihooThe biggest advantage of the SyncroFlex is when multiple people use the same chair. The ideal setup for one person rarely works for another. But because the Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 reads spine curvature on the fly rather than relying on presets, the same chair works for everyone.Self-Adaptive Dynamic Lumbar Support 2.0 and 8D bionic armrestsSihooThe lumbar system features three selectable support modes – Firm Lumbar Support, Gentle Lumbar Support, and Sacrum Support – aimed at different body types and personal preferences. You’ll also find extra width and a dedicated pressure-relief spring to support larger users. And the lumbar pad slides down with you as you recline, keeping contact with your sacrum through the motion.The armrests get a similarly detailed set of adjustments.
paragraph3: They move 85mm up and down, 40mm forward and back, and tilt 20 degrees downward for typing, which keeps your elbows supported and your shoulders from creeping up during long typing sessions. The rear section flips up 36 degrees with a 40-degree upward tilt, useful for resting your elbows during handheld gaming or reading on a tablet.They also shift 125mm side to side with inward and outward rotation, so they can line up with a desk that isn’t perfectly centered or match your arm angle rather than forcing your arm to match the armrest. When you recline, the armrests move with the chair and tilt up to 40 degrees further, keeping your arms supported through the motion.Headrest, seat, and recline positionsSihooThe Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 has an ultra-Wide 3D headrest that follows your neck as it moves, whether you’re leaning forward to read a screen or turning your head slightly. This addresses a common headrest problem you’ll find with other chairs: the pad supports you correctly in only one fixed position and leaves your neck unsupported the moment you shift.Underneath the chair, a Smart Weight-Adaptive Mechanism automatically adjusts recline resistance to your body weight, so the recline always feels smooth and controlled, without needing to manually tune the tension knob most chairs rely on.SihooThe seat itself uses a pressure-minimized cushion designed to spread weight evenly across your thighs and hips, paired with roughly 1.97 inches of seat depth adjustment. title: Pine Labs Appoints Ex-Amazon, Razorpay Executive Jayaram Karthik As COO
title_bn: পাইন ল্যাবস প্রাক্তন অ্যামাজন, রেজারপে নির্বাহী জয়রাম কার্তিককে সিওও হিসেবে নিয়োগ করেছে
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Fintech platform Pine Labs has appointed ex-Razorpay SVP Jayaram Karthik as its COO, as the company looks to strengthen its…
paragraph1: SUMMARYPine Labs has appointed Jayaram Karthik as its COO, with the veteran executive set to oversee operations and merchant experience across India and international markets. The appointment comes as Pine Labs looks to strengthen its operational infrastructure and standardise merchant journeys across its global footprint of more than 20 countries. Karthik brings more than 25 years of experience across operations, risk, analytics and technology, with leadership stints at American Express, Citibank, Amazon, Tata, and Razorpay. Fintech platform Pine Labs has appointed ex-Razorpay SVP Jayaram Karthik as its COO, as the company looks to strengthen its operational capabilities and support its next phase of growth. Karthik will lead operations and merchant experiences across India and Pine Labs’ international markets. His mandate will include building technology-enabled operating models aimed at creating seamless, trusted and locally relevant experiences for merchants. Prior to joining Pine Labs, Karthik served as the SVP of business operations for rival payments startup Razorpay for over half a decade.
paragraph2: Before that, he held senior operating roles at American Express, Citibank, Amazon, and Tata Play. Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau said the fintech’s future growth will depend not only on its products but also on how effectively technology and operations are integrated to deliver customer experiences. The company currently operates across more than 20 countries, making operational standardisation increasingly important as it expands its global footprint, Rau added. Karthik said his focus at Pine Labs would be on simplifying customer experiences by bringing technology, operations, and experience together. The appointment comes as Pine Labs continues to build its international presence. Its international business grew at a 44% CAGR over the past three years and contributed around 15% of revenue in FY26. Its international revenue crossed ₹400 Cr during the year.
paragraph3: In FY26, the company reported revenue from operations of ₹2,711 Cr, up 19% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA rose 57% to ₹559 Cr. It reported a net profit of ₹113 Cr as against a loss of ₹145 Cr in FY25. In the June quarter of the ongoing fiscal, its consolidated revenue from operations rose 19.6% YoY to ₹736.9 Cr, while net profit more than quadrupled to ₹19.6 Cr. Sequentially, the company’s profit declined 67% from ₹59.
paragraph4: 4 Cr. Pine Labs has also been expanding its product portfolio. It recently launched the Pine Labs Payment Protocol (P3P), which is an infrastructure layer allowing AI agents to make UPI payments autonomously after a consumer authorises a mandate. The company is also working to extend the protocol to card payments. It has also developed SignalIQ, an AI-powered bank statement analyser and underwriting engine. Pine Labs is also looking to embed AI across both its internal operations and customer-facing products. The company invested around ₹24 Cr in AI and R&D initiatives in FY26, including ₹20 Cr towards AI capabilities, technology infrastructure and process automation, and another ₹4 Cr on technologies such as MCP and RAG.
paragraph5: These investments have helped cut software testing cycle times by more than 95%, while Pine Labs estimates a 25% improvement in developer productivity and an 80% reduction in initial incident analysis time. Shares of Pine Labs ended today’s trading session 1.5% higher at ₹162.25 on the BSE.

bangla_paragraph3: ২৬ অর্থবছরে, সংস্থাটি ₹ ২,৭১১ কোটি অপারেশন থেকে আয় করেছে, যা বছরে ১৯% বৃদ্ধি পেয়েছে, যখন সমন্বিত ইবিআইটিডিএ ৫৭% বৃদ্ধি পেয়ে ৫৫৯ কোটি টাকা হয়েছে। এটি আর্থিক বছরে ১৪৫ কোটি টাকার ক্ষতির তুলনায় ১১৩ কোটি টাকায় নিট মুনাফা করেছে। চলমান আর্থিক বছরের জুন ত্রৈমাসিকে, অপারেশনের থেকে তার একীভূত আয় ১৯.৬% বৃদ্ধি পায় ₹ ৭৩৬.৯ কোটি টাকাতে, যখন নিট লাভ চারগুণেরও বেশি বেড়ে ১৯.৯৬ কোটি টকায় পৌঁছেছে। পরপর, কোম্পানির মুনাফায় ৫৯ থেকে ৬৭% হ্রাস পেয়েছে।

title: Is Russia's rival to Starlink failing? Here's what we know.
title_bn: স্টারলিংকের প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বী রাশিয়া কি ব্যর্থ হচ্ছে?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: At least three of the first 32 Rassvet satellites likely suffered outright failures, and more may be in trouble.
paragraph1: Some technical anomalies were expected. About 5 percent of SpaceX’s first batch of Starlinks failed almost immediately after launch. Over time, this group of 60 Starlink prototypes suffered a failure rate of about 13 percent, according to McDowell. With more experience, SpaceX’s next 420 Starlink satellites had a failure rate of about 3 percent. SpaceX’s current generation of Starlink Version 2 satellites has a failure rate of about 0.
paragraph2: 01 percent, according to McDowell’s tabulations. The US military’s Space Development Agency is fielding its own constellation of data relay satellites for applications in missile targeting and command and control. Some of the agency’s first 42 operational satellites encountered thermal and propulsion problems after launching last year, and they have taken longer than anticipated to raise their orbits. In its assessment on Monday, the Institute for the Study of War wrote that the second batch of Rassvet satellites “appears to have failed to reach intended operational altitudes.” Zero Rassvets have reached 500 miles, and none of the second group have climbed above 300 miles, whereas much of the first cluster seems to have settled into stable orbits.
paragraph3: However, there’s a lot we don’t know. Perhaps, for untold reasons, Russian officials decided to abandon plans to orbit the Rassvet satellites at 500 miles. Starlink satellites, after all, fly closer to 300 miles. This would put the Rassvet satellites closer to users on the ground, which comes with performance benefits. But there’s a trade-off in that lower-altitude constellations require more satellites for seamless global coverage.
paragraph4: Also, networks like Starlink, Rassvet, and China’s Guowang and Qianfan fly their satellites in numerous orbital planes, or pathways. Russian ground teams may be intentionally keeping some of the Rassvet satellites at lower altitudes to allow their orbital planes to drift over a period of many months before eventually lining up with final pathways. What we do know is that putting a megaconstellation into orbit is hard to do. At best, Russia’s entire satellite manufacturing sector has produced just a few dozen spacecraft per year since the fall of the Soviet Union. “It turned out we weren’t ready for this,” Yuri Borisov, the former head of Russia’s space agency, Roscosmos, said in an interview in 2023.
paragraph5: Russian forces are clamoring for Rassvet after SpaceX cut off access in February to the Starlink network by unregistered user terminals in Ukraine, circumventing Russia’s illicit use of satellite communications for military operations. Rassvet had been in the works for years, but the timing of the first Rassvet launch the following month offered Russian military commanders hope of soon regaining access to ubiquitous satellite broadband through a domestic network.

bangla_paragraph2: ম্যাকডওয়েল এর টেবিলিং অনুযায়ী, এই উপগ্রহের গতির হার ১.১ শতাংশ। মার্কিন সামরিক মহাকাশ উন্নয়ন সংস্থা ক্ষেপণাস্ত্র লক্ষ্যবস্তু এবং কমান্ড এবং নিয়ন্ত্রণে অ্যাপ্লিকেশনগুলির জন্য নিজস্ব ডাটা রিলে উপগ্রহগুলির একটি নক্ষত্রমণ্ডল স্থাপন করছে। সংস্থাটির প্রথম ৪২ টি অপারেশনাল উপগ্রহ গত বছর প্রবর্তনের পরে তাপীয় এবং প্রোপুলশন সমস্যার মুখোমুখি হয়েছিল এবং তাদের কক্ষপথ বাড়াতে প্রত্যাশিত সময়ের চেয়ে বেশি সময় লেগেছে। সোমবার তার মূল্যায়নে ইনস্টিটিউট ফর স্টাডি অফ ওয়ার লিখেছে যে দ্বিতীয় ব্যাচটি
bangla_paragraph3: তবে, আমরা অনেক কিছুই জানি না। সম্ভবত, অজানা কারণে, রাশিয়ান কর্মকর্তারা রাসভেট উপগ্রহগুলিকে ৫০০ মাইলের কক্ষপথে রাখার পরিকল্পনা পরিত্যাগ করার সিদ্ধান্ত নিয়েছেন। স্টারলিংক উপগ্রহ, সর্বোপরি, ৩০০ মাইলের কাছাকাছি উড়ে। এটি রাসভেত উপগ্রহকে স্থল ব্যবহারকারীদের কাছে আরও কাছাকাজি করবে, যা কর্মক্ষমতা সুবিধার সাথে আসে। তবে কম উচ্চতার নক্ষত্রমণ্ডলগুলিতে আরও বেশি উপগ্রহের প্রয়োজন যাতে নিরবচ্ছিন্ন বিশ্বব্যাপী কভারেজ থাকে।
bangla_paragraph4: এছাড়াও, স্টারলিংক, রাসভেট, এবং চীনের গুয়াং এবং কিয়ানফান এর মতো নেটওয়ার্কগুলি তাদের উপগ্রহগুলিকে অসংখ্য কক্ষপথের সমতল বা পথগুলিতে উড়তে দেয়। রাশিয়ান গ্রাউন্ড টিমগুলি তাদের কক্ষপথে প্লেনগুলি চূড়ান্ত পথের সাথে সারিবদ্ধ হওয়ার আগে কয়েক মাসের সময় ধরে ড্রিফট করার অনুমতি দেওয়ার জন্য রাশিয়ার কিছু রাসভেত উপগ্রহকে ইচ্ছাকৃতভাবে কম উচ্চতায় রেখেছে। আমরা যা জানি তা হ'ল কক্ষপাশে একটি মেগা কনস্টেলেশন স্থাপন করা কঠিন। সর্বোত্তম ক্ষেত্রে, রাশিয়ায় পুরো উপগ্রহ উত্পাদন খাতটি jus
bangla_paragraph5: রাশিয়ান বাহিনী রাসভেটের জন্য চিৎকার করছে, কারণ স্পেসএক্স ফেব্রুয়ারিতে ইউক্রেনের নিবন্ধিত ব্যবহারকারী টার্মিনালগুলিকে স্টারলিংক নেটওয়ার্কে অ্যাক্সেস বন্ধ করে দিয়েছে, রাশিয়ার সামরিক অভিযানের জন্য উপগ্রহ যোগাযোগের অবৈধ ব্যবহারকে এড়িয়ে দিয়েছে। রাসভেত বহু বছর ধরে কাজ করে আসছে, তবে পরের মাসে প্রথম রাসভিট উৎক্ষেপণের সময়সূচী রাশিয়ায় সামরিক কমান্ডারদের আশা দিয়েছে যে তারা শীঘ্রই একটি দেশীয় নেটওয়ার্ক মাধ্যমে সর্বব্যাপী উপগ্রহ ব্রডব্যান্ডে অ্যাকসেস ফিরে পাবে।

paragraph1: Wednesday September 2, 2026 3:17 am PDT by Tim HardwickLongtime leaker Sonny Dickson has shared an image of differently colored SIM card trays that he claims are for Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models, suggesting Apple's flagship lineup will again be available in a trio of colors: Silver, Dark Cherry, and Sky Blue. Apple currently offers the iPhone 17 Pro in Cosmic Orange, Silver, and Deep Blue. Dickson shared the image in response to a MacRumors report on Tuesday covering a Chinese leaker's claim that the iPhone 18 Pro models could come in Dark Cherry, Sky Blue, and Black. Dickson told MacRumors the colors in the shared image are the only ones he's come across in recent months. However, the leaker did share iPhone 18 Pro dummy units back in May that included a fourth Black color.
paragraph2: When that was pointed out to him, Dickson argued that black dummies are made every year, but it's not a color Apple prefers to use anymore. iPhone models sold in the U.S., Canada, and several other regions use eSIMs and don't come with SIM card trays, but devices sold in Europe, Japan, China, and Australia still include one (with the exception of the iPhone Air, which lacked a SIM tray everywhere it was sold). Chinese leaker Instant Digital in April said there would be no black color for the iPhone 18 Pro.
paragraph3: Last year was the first time Apple's high-end iPhones have not been available with a black or dark gray color option in any way, so it's possible Apple will continue that trend. Macworld reported in the same month that Apple would offer Light Blue, Dark Cherry, Dark Gray, and Silver colors. We'll know either way soon enough. title: Quick Commerce Supply Chain Startup DocPharma Nets $2 Mn For Expansion
title_bn: দ্রুত বাণিজ্য সরবরাহ চেইন স্টার্টআপ ডকফার্মা নেটস $2 মিলিয়ন সম্প্রসারণের জন্য
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Healthcare supply chain startup DocPharma has raised $2 Mn (₹19 Cr) in a Pre-Series A funding round led by Equentis,…
paragraph1: SUMMARYHealthcare supply chain startup DocPharma has raised $2 Mn (₹19 Cr) in a Pre-Series A funding round led by Equentis The development comes at a time when vertical quick commerce has been seeing a rapid growth, specifically in areas of quick pharma deliveries The startup plans to use the fresh capital to fuel expansion to 50 cities across India as well as setting up 100 new licensed dark stores Healthcare supply chain startup DocPharma has raised $2 Mn (₹19 Cr) in a Pre-Series A funding round led by Equentis, with participation from existing backer 100Unicorns, along with angel investment network Vinners and a host of undisclosed angel investors. The startup plans to use the fresh capital to fuel expansion to 50 cities across India as well as setting up 100 new licensed dark stores. Founded by Saquib Ali, Shashank Rai and Sagar Chauhan in 2024, DocPharma operates a quick commerce supply chain network catering to healthcare businesses, acting as a backend infrastructure for healthcare platforms.
paragraph2: At its core is its proprietary platform, DocPharma One, which combines warehouse management, inventory intelligence, order management and fulfillment operations. Its dark stores carry more than 40,000 SKUs each and are supported by an AI-driven and pharmacist-led compliance infrastructure. Its network of licensed dark stores and SaaS platform enables pharmacies, health insurers, hospitals, D2C wellness and nutraceutical brands, and pet care businesses to fulfil healthcare orders in under 30 minutes.
paragraph3: The startup claims that its infrastructure enables the delivery of medicines and healthcare products without requiring partner platforms to build and operate their own supply chains. “We built this supply chain rule by rule, one licensed dark store at a time, and that discipline is what lets it hold up as we scale into 50 cities,” Rai said. Currently, DocPharma operates across more than 12 cities and claims to have fulfilled over 8 Lakh orders with a fulfilment rate of more than 95%.
paragraph4: The development comes at a time when vertical quick commerce has been seeing a rapid growth, specifically in areas of quick pharma deliveries. Investors are also bullish in expansion of these businesses. For instance, quick medicine delivery startup Plazza raised $15 Mn in a Series A funding round to strengthen its technology platform and deepen its AI-led inventory and assortment capabilities.

title: Apple CEO John Ternus sends first memo to employees, teases ‘phenomenal’ 9 September launch
title_bn: অ্যাপলের প্রধান নির্বাহী জন টার্নাস কর্মীদের প্রথম মেমো পাঠিয়েছেন, প্রতিম ৯ সেপ্টেম্বর লঞ্চের কথা বলেছেন
author: TechPulse
excerpt: John Ternus officially becomes Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook as Executive Chairman, sending his first employee memo teasing a ‘phenomenal’ 9 September launch, as Johny Srouji is promoted to Chief Hardware Officer amid Apple's broader leadership resh
paragraph1: John Ternus officially becomes Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook as Executive Chairman, sending his first employee memo teasing a ‘phenomenal’ 9 September launch, as Johny Srouji is promoted to Chief Hardware Officer amid Apple's broader leadership reshuffle.Apple CEO John Ternus.John Ternus has officially taken over as Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook, who has transitioned to Executive Chairman. In his first letter to the employees, Ternus thanked everyone for their support and expressed his appreciation for Cook's leadership, calling him a “leader who led Apple with values, decency, and humanity.” The memo was sent to employees on the first day that Ternus became CEO, MacRumors reports.The message contained a short preview of Apple's near future.
paragraph2: Employees were told by Ternus that Apple had a “huge launch next week” that would be ‘phenomenal’, a reference widely interpreted as the company's 9 September “Surprise and Shine” event, where the iPhone 18 series is expected to be unveiled. While he did not mention any product by name, he said he was equally excited about the products already in development and those Apple has yet to imagine.Ternus highlights Apple’s future roadmapIn the memo, Ternus described Apple as the “greatest company in the world” and believes the company could “continue to be great with the same team.” He expressed his appreciation to the staff for their efforts in developing future products and stressed the need for further innovation in collaboration with the staff.In a statement on MacRumors, Ternus explained that there was “no team in the world” he would prefer to build the future with. His comments indicate that Apple is seeking to keep things consistent while also anticipating future products and technologies.
paragraph3: Leadership changes underway at AppleTernus brings a strong product-development background to the CEO role. He has been with Apple since 2001, and his last position before his departure was Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering, where he oversaw the manufacturing of key products for the company.Apple has restructured various teams as part of the leadership change. Johny Srouji has also been promoted to Chief Hardware Officer, where he will take over the hardware engineering division from Ternus. Apple has also reorganised its product design team, and former engineering vice president Laura Legros will be joining the company.First major test comes at the September eventThe event on 9 September will be the first time Ternus serves as CEO for an Apple product launch.
paragraph4: It's likely the event will feature the iPhone 18 lineup and other new devices and therefore is an influential occasion for Apple's brand-new management era.Before stepping down as CEO, Cook praised Ternus in a message to employees, saying he took “enormous comfort” in handing over leadership to someone he described as "brilliant", "wonderful", and "capable". As Apple prepares to release one of its most significant products of the year, it's only natural that the spotlight is now on Ternus as he begins to move the company forward.About the AuthorPragya Singha RoyPragya is a Technology reporter with over four years of experience in digital media and content writing. She holds a Master’s degree in Journalism and has covered a wide range of stories spanning space, smartphones, gadgets, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and the ways technology is transforming everyday life. She focuses on breaking down complex technology and science developments into clear, engaging, and reader-friendly stories, with a keen interest in emerging trends and their real-world impact.
paragraph5: Before joining her current newsroom, Pragya worked with News9Live, where she covered the technology beat extensively, reporting on smartphones, consumer technology, AI, space and science, while also contributing to video and visual content. Her experience includes breaking news, explainers, SEO-driven stories, product coverage, interviews, unboxing videos and live event reporting. She has also covered major technology and AI events, giving her experience in both newsroom and on-ground reporting. Beyond journalism, Pragya is an avid gamer and a passionate reader of fiction. She enjoys exploring immersive worlds through games and books, with a particular interest in stories that offer new perspectives, ideas, and experiences.

bangla_paragraph3: অ্যাপল টার্নাসে নেতৃত্বের পরিবর্তনগুলি সিইওর ভূমিকায় একটি শক্তিশালী পণ্য বিকাশের পটভূমি নিয়ে আসে। তিনি ২০০১ সাল থেকে অ্যাপলে ছিলেন এবং তার প্রস্থানের আগে তার শেষ পদে ছিলেন হার্ডওয়্যার ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিংয়ের সিনিয়র ভাইস প্রেসিডেন্ট, যেখানে তিনি সংস্থার মূল পণ্যগুলির উত্পাদন তদারকি করেছিলেন। নেতৃত্ব পরিবর্তনের অংশ হিসাবে অ্যাপল বিভিন্ন দলকে পুনর্গঠন করেছে। জননি শ্রুজিকে প্রধান হার্ডওয়ার অফিসার হিসাবে পদোন্নতি দেওয়া হয়েছে, যেখানে  থেকে তিনি হার্ডওয়ার ইঞ্জিনিয়ার্স বিভাগটি গ্রহণ করবেন।
bangla_paragraph4: সম্ভবত এই ইভেন্টে আইফোন ১৮ লাইনআপ এবং অন্যান্য নতুন ডিভাইস থাকবে এবং তাই অ্যাপলের ব্র্যান্ড নতুন ম্যানেজমেন্ট যুগের জন্য এটি একটি প্রভাবশালী অনুষ্ঠান।সিইও হিসাবে পদত্যাগ করার আগে, কুক কর্মীদের কাছে একটি বার্তায় টার্নাসের প্রশংসা করেছিলেন, তিনি বলেছিলেন যে তিনি "উজ্জ্বল", "আশ্চর্যজনক" এবং "ক্ষম" হিসাবে বর্ণনা করেছেন এমন কাউকে নেতৃত্ব দেওয়ার জন্য তিনি "অত্যন্ত স্বাচ্ছন্দ্য" পেয়েছিলেন। অ্যাপল বছরের অন্যতম গুরুত্বপূর্ণ পণ্য প্রকাশের প্রস্তুতি নিচ্ছে, তাই এটি স্বাভাবিক যে এখন টার্নেসের উপর স্পটলাইট রয়েছে কারণ তিনি
bangla_paragraph5: প্রজ্ঞার বর্তমান নিউজরুমে যোগদানের আগে, তিনি নিউজ৯লাইভ-এ কাজ করেছিলেন, যেখানে তিনি প্রযুক্তি বীটকে ব্যাপকভাবে কভার করেছিলেন, স্মার্টফোন, ভোক্তা প্রযুক্তি, এআই, মহাকাশ এবং বিজ্ঞান সম্পর্কে রিপোর্ট করেছিলেন, পাশাপাশি ভিডিও এবং ভিজ্যুয়াল সামগ্রীতে অবদান রেখেছিলেন। তার অভিজ্ঞতার মধ্যে রয়েছে ব্রেকিং নিউজ, ব্যাখ্যাকারী, এসইও-চালিত গল্প, পণ্য কভারেজ, সাক্ষাত্কার, আনবক্সিং ভিডিও এবং লাইভ ইভেন্ট রিপোর্টিং। তিনি প্রধান প্রযুক্তি এবং এআই ইভেন্টেও কভার করেছেন, নিউজ রুম এবং মাঠের রিপোর্টের উভয় ক্ষেত্রেই তার অভিজ্ঞতা দিয়েছেন।

paragraph1: Wednesday September 2, 2026 1:35 am PDT by Tim HardwickApple last month announced a new Mac mini and a new Mac Studio. Both machines start shipping on Tuesday, September 22, which means they will launch in the same month as new iPhones, Apple Watches, and AirPods. Apple is expected to introduce the unannounced products at its annual iPhone fall event, which is this year carrying the tagline "Surprise and shine." The event takes place on Wednesday, September 9, making this month one of the busiest Apple has had in a while. We should therefore see eight new Apple products go on sale before the end of September: Mac mini (M6 and M5 Pro): Announced last week, the new models start shipping September 22, with prices starting at $899. Mac Studio (M5 Max and M5 Ultra): Also announced last week, the new models begin shipping September 22, with prices starting at $2,499. iPhone 18 Pro: The flagship device set to be unveiled at Apple's fall event, with a smaller Dynamic Island and a A20 Pro chip. iPhone 18 Pro Max: The device is rumored to gain a camera upgrade exclusive to the larger model, alongside a bigger battery.
paragraph2: Foldable iPhone: The company's first foldable is expected to have a ~5.5-inch display when closed, and a ~7.8-inch display when open, plus a super thin design with minimal crease and a durable hinge. It could be called "iPhone Ultra." Apple Watch Series 12: Apple's upcoming smartwatch is expected feature fitness tracking improvements and a faster S12 chip. Apple Watch Ultra 4: Apple's flagship rugged watch is expected to be updated alongside the Series 12, gaining the same S12 chip. AirPods 5: The new earbuds were referenced in macOS 26.7 and are reportedly ready for release, suggesting a launch alongside the new iPhones.
paragraph3: Apple isn't going to release a standard iPhone 18 in September 2026. The lineup will instead focus on more expensive iPhones. The ‌iPhone 18‌, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 will come out in spring 2027 instead. Apple does not plan to refresh the Apple Watch SE this year. Apple has held its fall event in the first two weeks of September in each of the last several years, with new iPhones going on sale the following Friday. Apple's "iPhone Ultra" was recently believed to have a delayed launch running into October, even though it's expected to be announced at the same time as the iPhone 18 Pro models. However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said this week he would be "very surprised" if the foldable did not come out at the same time as the Pro iPhones or "very close to it." "Either on the same launch date, a dual launch, or coming out within weeks later.
paragraph4: This idea of a late October, November launch, massive delays, supply chain issues, I don't believe to be the case," he said. Note that the Mac Studio configuration with 512GB of unified memory is coming in late October rather than on September 22. Every other Mac Studio configuration ships in September. While it was initially rumored that Touch ID may be coming to the Apple Watch this year, Gurman reiterated that he does not expect the Series 12 or Ultra 4 to have any major design changes compared to the current Series 11 and Ultra 3 models.
